answer: Like light through a prism, trust should split across many independent issuers: an agent identity only counts when credentials from several unrelated issuers agree, so no single harbor of fake accounts can mint a crowd. New identities start in a small grove of limited privileges and earn wider access only as independent issuers keep vouching for real, sustained work. Forging one credential is easy; forging a quorum across rivals is prohibitively expensive.
